summary: This note is a short encyclopedia-style overview of the history of sport in several ancient civilizations. It covers evidence of early sport in China, regulated sports depicted in ancient Egypt, and sports with military links that originated in ancient Persia. The passage is brief and focuses on antiquity rather than modern sport.
one_line: Overview of sport in ancient China, Egypt and Persia, from early gymnastics and swimming to polo and jousting.
key_facts: Artifacts and structures suggest sport in China existed as early as 2000 BC.
Gymnastics appears to have been popular in China's ancient past.
Monuments to the Pharaohs indicate that swimming and fishing were well-developed and regulated several thousands of years ago in ancient Egypt.
Other Egyptian sports included javelin throwing, high jump, and wrestling.
Ancient Persian sports had a close connection to warfare skills.
The traditional Iranian martial art of Zourkhaneh is an ancient Persian sport with a close connection to warfare skills.
